nodes.label: publish workflow
nodes.rationale: Fires when a GitHub Release is published, with a workflow_dispatch fallback because a release-event run uses the workflow file at the tag's commit, so a workflow bug cannot be fixed and re-run through the release event alone. Typecheck/test/build are deliberately not separate steps - npm publish runs prepublishOnly (clean, build, typecheck, test) on the same Bun toolchain immediately before publishing.

nodes.label: npm Trusted Publishing via OIDC
nodes.rationale: No long-lived NPM_TOKEN: the workflow exchanges its short-lived OIDC token for a one-shot publish token, requiring npm >= 11.5.1 (bundled with Node 24, the engines floor) and a Trusted Publisher registered for the repo and this workflow file. id-token: write serves both provenance and OIDC auth - which is also why every uses: is SHA-pinned, since those actions run in the same job as a credential that can publish to npm with provenance.

nodes.label: Already-published version guard
nodes.rationale: npm view decides whether to skip, making re-runs safe. It is a check-then-act, so two overlapping runs would both see not published and the loser would die on npm's E403, which reads like a broken release; the concurrency group serialises them instead - not cancel-in-progress, because an in-flight npm publish is the last thing to interrupt.

nodes.label: CycloneDX SBOM generation job
nodes.rationale: --provenance answers who built the tarball but says nothing about what is inside the closure, and GitHub's dependency graph cannot reconstruct it (#539). Syft catalogues node_modules/ after a frozen install rather than reading the Bun lockfile, because a bill of materials assembled from unresolved ranges looks authoritative and names versions nobody shipped. examples, docs and tests are deleted first: ten manifests the package does not ship would otherwise appear as though they did - and those npm lockfiles are exactly where every Dependabot alert comes from, making the document actively misleading. dependency-snapshot is off so a release closure is not reported as the default branch's state.

nodes.label: SBOM release-asset upload job
nodes.rationale: No checkout and no install - that is the point of the split; its only act with contents: write is uploading one file. Skipped for workflow_dispatch re-runs, which have no release to attach to, and --clobber so a re-attempt does not die on asset already exists.

nodes.label: SBOM build/upload privilege split
nodes.rationale: Generating the SBOM needs the installed tree and uploading a release asset needs contents: write; one job would hold a credential that can push to the repository while running the postinstall scripts of the entire dependency tree. WorkflowHygiene.test.ts fails on exactly that combination since #622, and the split is the right answer rather than an exemption. Neither job is a dependency of publish, so a broken SBOM can never block shipping.
